items.title: Loretta Rowland Evans Interview, 1967-06-01
items.q: The transcript mentions 'sister Kelly' only in the interviewer's prompt ('You're saying sister Kelly...') but the interviewee does not respond to or elaborate on this specific person in the provided text. The interviewee's speech focuses on bands, Lewis Prima, and the history of music venues.

ctx.x: Every town and village had its own orchestra. When you attended a movie or a Broadway show, bands played in the pits. As it was called, another stage built in from the picture screen. Instead, such gage could be lowered to any level, but a band would play there. I remember Lewis Prima at the Sangers in said band. That's how he became famous. He surely could play like trumpet and jazz. I stayed for two shows and I went every week just to hear him play. And he really played jazz and he is still playing. 1926 was…

You were saying something about that, the cemetery, it was Lafayette number one? Yeah, I have it here. You want that in it? Oh, I'd love to know about that funeral. That sounds like something I never heard of before. That knocking on the coffin. Yeah. You're saying sister Kelly...
